title: A feasible reaction schedule does not certify blind asynchronous reliability
statement: With independent identical exponential first-success clocks activated simultaneously and irreversible pairwise blockers i->j, completion probability is the number of orders satisfying j-before-i for every edge divided by n!. A blocking chain on three sites gives1/6. For the cooperative triple with a safe second port only at site2, exactly the two orders ending in2 succeed: probability1/3 despite a release-free feasible plan.

requires: Specified independent simultaneous first-success clocks, no other chemical failures, irreversible retained footprints and a supplied static port map.
provides: With independent identical exponential first-success clocks activated simultaneously and irreversible pairwise blockers i->j, completion probability is the number of orders satisfying j-before-i for every edge divided by n!. assumptions: The n! denominator requires identical rates; unequal rates, physical activation dependencies and random guide release change the process.
Deterministic schedule existence and bond-observing execution are distinct from blind stochastic reliability.
costs: All staged attempts, time, rate control and residual misses; no zero-cost perfect order selection.
contract.units: Clock rates have inverse-time units, permutation probabilities dimensionless; a finite-order model is not a chemical throughput experiment.
contract.obstruction: Acquire actual first-success/activation laws or product-qualified staging before claiming reliable execution.

body: Identical independent continuous clocks induce a uniform permutation. Completion under irreversible retained footprints is exactly the event that this permutation respects all block constraints; any blocked clock event leaves an unfinished site forever. For unequal positive constant rates the probability of a permutation is the product of each next rate divided by the remaining total rate, not1/n!. The actual source hyperblock branch checks legal ports along each sampled order; its pairwise branch equivalently forbids firing a blocker before any unfinished target. An independent blocking pair succeeds with probability1/2; multiplying over500 independent pairs gives2^(-500), only under that cross-pair independence. Harmless repeated chemistry changes nothing if effective first-success clocks keep the stated law. Outcome-confirmed staging can choose an order; blind finite staging pays missed-attempt probabilities and cannot assume persistent dead sites recover.
